title: $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ is a triangulated subcategory
statement:
Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ contains $0$, is closed under shifts in both directions and
under isomorphisms, and if $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ is a distinguished triangle in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
with two of $K,L,M$ in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, then so is the third. Hence $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ is a full
triangulated subcategory.

Here $\ell$ is a prime, $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and $X$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]; $\Qlb$ is an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ is a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. The coefficient ring is the pulled-back condensed ring $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$, as in [def-sfb-subfield-coefficient-ring] and [def-sfb-qlbar-coefficient-ring], and $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ is the category of module objects of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. The ambient $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is the ordinary derived category [pur713-def-module-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the constructible modules of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The full subcategory $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ consists of modules isomorphic to small filtered colimits, computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, of objects of $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$. Finally,
$$
\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}) : H^n(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for every }n\in\mathbf Z\}.
$$
Full triangulated subcategory has the meaning of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

proof.text: The zero module is constructible: on each affine open use the single stratum and the zero finitely presented scalar module in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. It is therefore ind-constructible, using the constant diagram on the one-object filtered category. The zero complex has $H^n(0)=0$ for every $n$, by the cohomology formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $0\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$. If $K\simeq L$, the cohomology functors carry this to $H^n(K)\simeq H^n(L)$ for every $n$; the definition of $\IndCons$ is invariant under isomorphisms. Thus $\Dic$ is closed under isomorphisms.

source.place: First sentence: zero; isomorphism closure made explicit

proof.text: For every $r,n\in\mathbf Z$, [lem-sp-derived-cohomology-shift] gives $H^n(K[r])\simeq H^{n+r}(K)$. Hence, when $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, every cohomology object of $K[r]$ is ind-constructible. This proves closure under all integer shifts, in particular both $[1]$ and $[-1]$.

Let $K\to L\to M\to K[1]$ be a distinguished triangle with $K,L\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] to the abelian category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ underlying the ordinary ambient derived category. For each $n$ it gives an exact segment
$$H^n(K)\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}H^n(L)\xrightarrow{u_n}H^n(M)\xrightarrow{v_n}H^{n+1}(K)\xrightarrow{\beta_n}H^{n+1}(L).$$

In this exact segment, $\ker u_n=\operatorname{im}\alpha_n$, so the universal properties of cokernels identify $\operatorname{coker}\alpha_n$ with $\operatorname{coker}(\ker u_n\hookrightarrow H^n(L))$, the coimage of $u_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coimage-mono], the induced map $\operatorname{coker}\alpha_n\to H^n(M)$ is monic, with image $\operatorname{im}u_n=\ker v_n$. The opposite of the ambient abelian category is abelian: the axioms in [def-sp-abelian] exchange kernels with cokernels and monomorphisms with epimorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coimage-mono] there to $v_n^{\mathrm{op}}$. Taking opposites gives an epimorphism $H^n(M)\twoheadrightarrow\ker(\operatorname{coker}v_n)$, which is $\operatorname{im}v_n=\ker\beta_n$ by exactness. Its kernel is $\ker v_n$, since the inclusion $\ker\beta_n\hookrightarrow H^{n+1}(K)$ is monic. Thus the preceding monomorphism is its kernel and there is a short exact sequence in the ambient abelian category:
$$0\longrightarrow\operatorname{coker}\alpha_n\longrightarrow H^n(M)\longrightarrow\ker\beta_n\longrightarrow0.$$
All kernels, images and cokernels here are ambient categorical ones.

source.place: Displayed short exact sequence: image and quotient argument made explicit

proof.text: All four objects $H^n(K),H^n(L),H^{n+1}(K),H^{n+1}(L)$ lie in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Since it is a full subcategory, $\alpha_n$ and $\beta_n$ are morphisms in it. By [det-ind-heart-kernels-cokernels], their ambient cokernel $\operatorname{coker}\alpha_n$ and kernel $\ker\beta_n$ lie in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Apply [det-ind-heart-extensions] to the short exact sequence of the preceding step. It yields $H^n(M)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. Since $n$ was arbitrary, $M\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Last sentence: kernels, cokernels and extension closure from the ind-heart proposition

proof.text:
Steps 3–5 established the following implication for every distinguished triangle $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$: if $A,B\in\Dic$, then $C\in\Dic$. Write the original triangle as $K\xrightarrow{a}L\xrightarrow{b}M\xrightarrow{c}K[1]$. TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] makes
$$L\xrightarrow{b}M\xrightarrow{c}K[1]\xrightarrow{-a[1]}L[1]$$
distinguished. If $L,M\in\Dic$, instantiate the proved implication with $(A,B,C)=(L,M,K[1])$ to obtain $K[1]\in\Dic$. Step 2 gives $(K[1])[-1]\in\Dic$, and the shift isomorphism $(K[1])[-1]\simeq K$ and step 1 give $K\in\Dic$. A second application of TR2 gives the distinguished triangle
$$M\xrightarrow{c}K[1]\xrightarrow{-a[1]}L[1]\xrightarrow{-b[1]}M[1].$$
If $K,M\in\Dic$, step 2 first gives $K[1]\in\Dic$. Instantiate the proved implication with $(A,B,C)=(M,K[1],L[1])$ to obtain $L[1]\in\Dic$; then step 2 gives $(L[1])[-1]\in\Dic$ and step 1 with $(L[1])[-1]\simeq L$ gives $L\in\Dic$.

source.place: By rotation it suffices to treat the third vertex: both cases made explicit

proof.text: By its defining object condition $\Dic$ is a full subcategory of the triangulated category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The preceding steps give its zero object, stability under every integer shift, and the middle-vertex extension property for distinguished triangles. These are exactly the criterion of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]; hence the inherited shifts and distinguished triangles make $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ a full triangulated subcategory.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof, with the zero/isomorphism arguments, the short exact sequence, and both rotations expanded
